data.narrative:
Astrolight, a seed-stage space & aerospace company founded by Laurynas Mačiulis, has raised €2.8M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 5 public-market peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for direct comparable application.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised (€2.8M, approximated as $3M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x yields $7M. This represents the core triangulation point given the limited data available at the seed stage. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 26.4x across the Space & Aerospace sector) cannot be deployed because target revenue is not disclosed. Peer-median analysis is similarly inapplicable; while 14 same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold criteria for adjacent-stage or similar-tier clustering needed for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M–$8M (median $7M) with substantial uncertainty. Key limitations include reliance on a single valuation method, absence of revenue or profitability data, and the nascent stage of the company. Investors should recognize this represents a provisional framework pending disclosure of operational metrics or comparable transaction data within the space-tech subsector.
